To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATF2 silences the growth inhibitory effect of tamoxifen and promotes cell proliferation in ER-positive, tamoxifen-resistant cells.
ATF2 is a key mediator of endocrine resistance and its knockdown can overcome resistance.
ATF2 silences ER and ER regulated genes in tamoxifen sensitive breast cancer cells and enhances ER and ER regulated gene expression in tamoxifen resistant cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of ATF2 as a key determinant of endocrine resistance in breast cancer and the development of novel therapeutic strategies to overcome resistance to endocrine therapy.
the role of ATF2 and its downstream targets in the regulation of ER activity and endocrine resistance.
the identification of new therapeutic targets in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATF2 silences ER and ER-regulatory gene expression, and that ATF2 knockdown enhances ER and ER-regulation of gene expression.
ATF2 is a key determinant for endocrine resistance in breast cancer.
ATF2 is a key determinant for the development of resistance to endocrinal treatments and that ATF2 is an important therapeutic target in the treatment of ER-positive breast cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATF2 is a key regulator of ER expression and activity in breast cancer and is a potential therapeutic target in endocrine resistant disease.
ATF2 silences ER expression, and thus, endocrine sensitivity, but in the presence of high levels of ER, ATF2 enhances ER transcriptional activity, thus, promoting endocrine resistance.
ATF2 silences ER in the sensitive MCF7 cells, but in TAMR it is ER that is silencing ATF2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeting ATF2 in ER positive breast cancer may be an effective therapeutic approach in the clinic.
ATF2 is a key determinant to the endocrine sensitivity of breast cancer cells.
ATF2 is a key regulator of endocrine sensitivity in breast cancer cells.
